classification.difficultyReason: Construct a two-set Venn diagram, then count outcomes for a union and a difference.

content.prompt: In a group of 200 students, 100 study geography, 60 study mathematics and 40 study both.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Represent this information on a Venn diagram.

answer.worked:
Let $G$ represent students studying geography and $M$ represent students studying mathematics.

There are 40 students in the intersection.

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Geography only}&=100-40=60\\\text{Mathematics only}&=60-40=20\\\text{Neither}&=200-(60+40+20)=80\end{aligned}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Review exercise question 10a; answer figure on teacher PDF page 33
spec.description: Unshaded universal rectangle containing overlapping sets G and M. The disjoint regions contain 60, 40 and 20, with 80 outside both circles.
spec.mathematics: Geography only 60; both 40; mathematics only 20; neither 80; total 200.
spec.answerVisibility: Complete solution figure shown only in answer editions.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If a student is selected at random from the group, what is the probability that the student studies:

children.label: i
children.prompt: at least one of these subjects?

answer.worked:
The three regions inside the circles contain $60+40+20=120$ students.

$$P(\text{at least one subject})=\frac{120}{200}=\frac{3}{5}.$$

The geography-only region contains $100-40=60$ students.

$$P(\text{geography but not mathematics})=\frac{60}{200}=\frac{3}{10}.$$
